headline: Medium-risk pair: shared file-based workflows can leak or corrupt content; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can read/write local files and uses stdin/stdout plus notebooks; Agent B is a chat bot over messaging channels. No shared channel or direct ingestion path is documented, so prompt injection is not default. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or file handoff, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into B's chat channel, B may follow injected instructions.
IF A writes attacker-controlled content into a file that B later parses as prompts, injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Avoid copying raw A outputs into B prompts.
Add a short human review step before forwarding content.
Use a fixed template when transferring text between agents.
Store A and B artifacts in separate folders.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared handoff channel.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches configuration secrets and writes to the filesystem; Agent B can receive messages through external channels like Slack or Telegram. A shared workspace is not stated, but file-based handoff or copied content could expose secrets or research data from A into B outputs. Because the interaction is plausible but undocumented, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF A stores secrets or paper metadata in a shared file that B reads, leakage can occur.
IF an operator forwards A's output into B's messaging channel, sensitive content may be exposed externally.
mitigations: Keep A secrets in a separate directory.
Redact secrets before any handoff to B.
Disable forwarding of raw logs to chat channels.
Review shared artifacts for credentials before use.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation between agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while B is a conversational bot with no write or git permissions listed. There is no documented shared mutable resource or overlapping write scope, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because shared-state behavior is not stated for A and B.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF B is extended with write access outside this profile, conflict severity increases.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Run only one writer at a time.
Use read-only mounts for B.
Check for existing files before A writes.
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces research and content-writing outputs that B could plausibly relay to users through chat channels. B is a customer-support bot, so if it treats A's text as authoritative, errors can cascade into user-facing answers. No verification step is documented, but B is not shown to take irreversible actions, so medium fits.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text as a response template without verification, misinformation can propagate.
IF A's research output is inserted into B's knowledge base, B may repeat errors at scale.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them.
Add source links to every transferred fact.
Reject uncited claims in B responses.
Limit B to summarizing, not asserting, A content.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before ingestion.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles configuration secrets and research materials; B handles text and voice with messaging integrations. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to generic handling gaps. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not directly evidenced, low is appropriate rather than none.
conditions: IF A secrets or research data are routed into B's external messaging integrations, retention and disclosure obligations may change.
IF either agent logs transcripts longer than intended, retention mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Minimize data sent from A to B.
Turn off transcript logging where possible.
Review retention settings in connected channels.
Separate secret-bearing workflows from support chat.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention for both agents.
